questions.stem: A virus is inactivated by ether. What can you conclude?
questions.explanation: Ether dissolves the lipid envelope; naked viruses resist it. A: Envelope, not nucleic acid type, determines sensitivity. B: Symmetry is unrelated. C: Prions aren't viruses and resist many agents. E: Replication site is unrelated.
Parvoviruses are the ssDNA exception. A, B, D: These are dsDNA. C: Reovirus is the dsRNA exception.

questions.stem: Hepatitis D virus can only replicate in cells co-infected with hepatitis B virus. HDV is therefore best described as a:
questions.explanation: Defective viruses need a helper virus (HBV supplies HBsAg). B: Prions lack nucleic acid. C: Viroids are naked RNA in plants. D: Pseudovirions carry host DNA. E: Bacteriophages infect bacteria.

questions.stem: How are naked (non-enveloped) viruses typically released from infected cells?
questions.explanation: Naked viruses exit by lysis. A, D: Budding is how enveloped viruses exit and acquire their envelope. B: Not the typical route. E: Conjugation is bacterial gene transfer.

questions.stem: A pandemic influenza strain emerges with hemagglutinin from an avian virus and other genes from a human virus. Which mechanism produced it?
questions.explanation: Influenza has a segmented RNA genome; co-infection allows segment swapping → shift. A: Drift gives minor seasonal changes. C: Recombination occurs mostly in DNA viruses. D: Interference blocks a second virus. E: Complementation supplies proteins without exchanging genes.

questions.stem: A man dies of encephalitis weeks after a bat bite. Which inclusion bodies are expected in his brain neurons?
questions.explanation: Rabies produces intracytoplasmic Negri bodies. A: Cowdry bodies are intranuclear (herpes). B: Combined inclusions are the measles pattern. C: Syncytia are a cell-fusion cytopathic effect, not inclusions. D: Plaques are foci of dead cells in tissue culture.

questions.stem: In retrovirus replication, which enzyme transcribes viral mRNA and progeny genomes from the integrated proviral DNA?
questions.explanation: After reverse transcription and integration, the provirus is transcribed by the host cell RNA polymerase. B: Reverse transcriptase makes DNA from the RNA genome, the earlier step. C: Retroviruses do not copy RNA from RNA. D: Integrase inserts the DNA but does not transcribe it. E: Retroviruses do not carry a DNA polymerase for transcription.

questions.stem: A virus is inoculated onto the chorioallantoic membrane of a 10-day embryonated egg. Which finding shows viral growth?

options.D: Pocks: white opaque areas on the membrane

questions.explanation: Pocks are white opaque lesions on the transparent CAM from virus-infected cells. A: Plaques are seen in tissue culture. B: Syncytia are a cytopathic effect in cell culture. C: Negri bodies are rabies inclusions in neurons. E: Mucoid colonies are capsulated bacteria on agar.

questions.stem: Herpesviruses and paramyxoviruses usually enter host cells by which mechanism?

options.B: Fusion of the envelope with the cell membrane via F protein

questions.explanation: These enveloped viruses carry F protein and fuse with the cell membrane, releasing the nucleocapsid into the cytoplasm. A: Direct penetration is the bacteriophage example. C: Endocytosis engulfs virions in vesicles; it is not the example given for these viruses. D: Budding is a release step. E: Lysis is how naked viruses are released.
